species.label: Bluefin tuna
species.note: Sport-fleet catch peaks at 63-70°F (Runcie 2019); in warmer surface water bluefin go deep, out of reach of surface gear.

species.label: Yellowfin tuna
species.note: Holds on the warm, clear side of fronts (Block 1997); a shallow mixed layer pushes it up.

species.label: Dorado (mahi)
species.note: The paddy fish: 75% of Mexican Pacific catch at chlorophyll 0.05-0.25 mg/m³ (Marín-Enríquez 2018).

species.label: Yellowtail (offshore, paddy fish)
species.note: San Diego catch rates rise at 64-68°F and fall above 69°F (Squire 1982; inshore fleet data).

species.label: Striped marlin
species.note: San Diego catch averaged 67.8°F; works breaks and blue water against green over the banks.

species.label: Wahoo
species.note: A warm-year visitor (CPFV: 42 in 2014, 256 in 2015); holds on banks and high spots.

fleet_recent.coverage_note: AIS is heard only within roughly 30-50 nm of shore receivers, and most boats under 65 ft never broadcast it.

inshore.label: Yellowtail (islands and kelp)
inshore.drivers: Warm-year regime (landings swing from under 10,000 to 450,000 fish), bait: squid, sardine, mackerel.
inshore.look: Outer kelp edge next to deep water, up-current points at the islands.
inshore.evidence: Strong for the regime; the 64-66°F 'switch' is angler lore.
inshore.today: Surface water is 73°F; San Diego catch rates have fallen above 69°F in fleet data.

inshore.label: White seabass
inshore.drivers: Spawning Mar-Jul (peak May); tagged fish spent half their time at 55-61°F, tracking the thermocline.
inshore.look: Kelp near squid grounds, at dusk; near the surface Apr-Oct, deeper Dec-Feb.
inshore.evidence: Thermal niche from one tagging study (Aalbers & Sepulveda 2015).
inshore.today: Surface water is 73°F, above the 55-61°F the tagged fish used; offshore, the nearest glider puts the thermocline about 151 ft down, and the cooler water they favored sits below it.

inshore.label: Calico (kelp) bass
inshore.drivers: Small home ranges; spawns Jun-Aug at 25-60 ft under kelp.

fishing.method: Profiles say where the water matches what each species needs, not how many fish are there. Water temperature is the satellite map's; breaks are the strongest gradient within 10 nm of a spot, read as the temperature change across 4.3 nm. A cue met at most in-range spots that day is 'everywhere' and singles nothing out.
fishing.counts_note: No dock counts: the network that publishes SoCal landing counts now forbids automated collection and republishing without a license.

bottom_line: Shore diving today: outside our thresholds at Point Loma and Sunset Cliffs and Laguna Beach; marginal at La Jolla Cove and La Jolla Shores. The San Diego County surf forecast is 3 to 5 feet from 210°, with a high rip current risk.

fishing: By boat today: marginal for the Coronados and the outer islands; within our thresholds for San Diego inshore, the offshore banks, and Catalina and the San Pedro Channel. Monday gets worse for the offshore banks and the outer islands (seas, NWS advisories and wind).
Water at the named spots runs 68-75°F on the Oct 15 satellite map; the strongest break is near San Clemente Island, 2.3°F over 4.3 nm, warm side to the NE.
Season and water both match today for bluefin tuna, yellowfin tuna, dorado, yellowtail, striped marlin and wahoo. That says the water is right, not that fish are there.
AIS shows 8 boats at sea in the last 3 hours, 1 of them stopped. Over the last three days the fleet stopped longest at 33.65N 118.17W.
diving: Shore diving today: outside our thresholds at Point Loma and Sunset Cliffs and Laguna Beach; marginal at La Jolla Cove and La Jolla Shores. The San Diego County surf forecast is 3 to 5 feet from 210°, with a high rip current risk.
Best bet from shore: La Jolla Shores (marginal, with sets around 0 ft at the entry in the CDIP model). Just Get Wet (La Jolla dive shop) reported 20-30 ft at La Jolla on Oct 17.

Suit: 3-5 mm for most divers, sized for 73°F at 60 ft in the nearest glider profile. Kelp-bed bottoms can run colder when internal tides push cold water in. A glider 14 nm from San Diego measured 73°F at the surface and 72°F at 100 ft, with the sharpest drop near 151 ft (10:26 PM Oct 17).
spearfishing: Entries today: outside our thresholds at Point Loma and Sunset Cliffs and Laguna Beach; marginal at La Jolla Cove and La Jolla Shores. The San Diego County surf forecast is 3 to 5 feet from 210°, with a high rip current risk.
Just Get Wet (La Jolla dive shop) reported 20-30 ft at La Jolla on Oct 17: enough to hunt pelagics (15 ft or more).

A glider 14 nm from San Diego measured 73°F at the surface and 72°F at 100 ft, with the sharpest drop near 151 ft (10:26 PM Oct 17). White seabass: Surface water is 73°F, above the 55-61°F the tagged fish used; offshore, the nearest glider puts the thermocline about 151 ft down, and the cooler water they favored sits below it. Open now: spiny lobster (by hand only).

synopsis.text: At 12 AM, a 1027 mb high was centered approximately 515 miles west of the CA/OR border over the Pacific Ocean, and a 1013 mb low was located over the Napa Valley area in central California. Weak offshore flow is expected through this early morning, with onshore flow returning by later day and onward, but may briefly turn weakly offshore again tonight. Southerly flow will increase Wednesday as a weather system arrives.
A moderate storm system is expected sometime Tuesday through Thursday.

headlines.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 18 at 12:59AM PDT until October 20 at 9:00AM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
headlines.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated
surf expected. Surf will build to 3 to 6 feet Sunday and persist
through Tuesday morning.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...From 9 AM PDT this morning through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor beach erosion and tidal overflows may
occur across south-facing beaches, especially in the Huntington
Beach area.
headlines.instruction:
Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.
